label: Aristotle, Metaphysics IV.7, 1012a2-4: Every act of thought that is true or false is an…
interpretation: Reading A (conditional) of 'every object of discursive and intuitive thought, thought either affirms or denies (this is clear from the definition) whenever it is true or false' (ὅταν ἀληθεύῃ ἢ ψεύδηται). The temporal clause is taken as a condition: every act of thought that is true or false is an affirmation or a denial, so there is no third act that is true or false. 'Clear from the definition' is read as the definition of truth and falsity at 1011b26-27. This reading excludes an intermediate that is true or false; it does not say that every object is in fact judged.
